Who benefits: Individual outdoor recreationists (hikers, climbers, kayakers) who travel in remote areas where other distress methods are impractical or unreliable.. In the government pilot, distribute 50 ACR PLBs to local emergency response agencies via existing procurement channels, offering the same hardware at the same price, emphasizing interoperability and long-range distress capability. Track actual purchase. Sample: Consumer pilot: 50 outdoor recreationists (hiking, kayaking, climbing) recruited via outdoor retailer partnerships. Government pilot: 50 emergency response personnel (police, fire, SAR) recruited via local department contacts.. Measure: Number of units purchased by each group within the 12‑week pilot period.. Predictions: T1: Consumer pilot will achieve at least 30 purchases (60% adoption rate), indicating outdoor recreationists adopt the beacon.; T2: Government pilot will achieve at least 25 purchases (50% adoption rate), indicating emergency responders and SAR teams adopt the beacon.. Decision rule: If consumer pilot purchases ≥30 and government pilot purchases <25, conclude T1 is better supported. If government pilot purchases ≥25 and consumer pilot purchases <30, conclude T2 is better supported. If both meet thresholds, both theories remain. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Based on medical evidence linking excess body fat to heart disease, diabetes and certain cancers, Tanita introduced the world’s first integrated body composition analyzer/scale to the professional markets in 1992.
Tanita is a world leader in precision electronic scales. With almost 50% of its domestic market share, the name Tanita is a household name in Japan.
In Japan, every household has a bathroom scale (health meter), and most nowadays keep track of your body composition.
In 104 men and 101 women (16-78 years and BMI 16-41 kg/m2) the mean bias in body-fat mass measured using the Tanita body-fat analyser was 0.8 (2SD 7.9) kg relative to a four-compartment model.
